For a point charge placed outside a grounded conducting sphere the electro‐static problem can be solved by the method of images.  
Let the real charge q be on the positive z–axis at a distance  

d  ( >d > R )  

from the centre O of the sphere (radius R).

Image system for a grounded sphere  
• Image charge: q′=−q R / d  
• Position of the image: at a distance a = R²/d from O on the same axis  
(The sphere’s surface potential is then identically zero.)

1. Potential at the position of the real charge produced by the image charge  
Distance between the real charge and the image charge:

r′ = d − a = d − R²/d = (d² − R²)/d.

Hence  

V_induced = k q′/r′  
           = k ( −q R/d ) / ( (d² − R²)/d )  
           = − k q R /(d² − R²).

2. Electrostatic energy of the configuration  
The energy stored in the fields equals

U = (1/2) q V_induced

because (i) we must exclude the infinite self–energy of the real charge and (ii) the grounded conductor is at zero potential, so its own surface charges give no contribution to ∫ρV dτ.

Therefore  

U = (1/2) q ( − k q R /(d² − R²) )  
   = − (1/2) k q² R /(d² − R²).

This matches choice (D).

Answer: D
